articles.title: Is Now the Time for a Reskilling Revolution?
articles.topic: 技能再培训势在必行：从公司到国家层面缓解技能不匹配
articles.source: 2021 年考研英语（二）Text 1 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind.
sentences.cn: "再培训"虽然听上去像个时髦词，但实际上，如果我们希望未来的劳动力不被大量抛弃，那它就是一件必须要做的事情。

words.meaning: n. 时髦用语，流行术语
adj. 想要成为……的，未来的

sentences.en: We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain.
sentences.cn: 众所周知，我们正步入这样一个时期：（社会）所需的工作岗位将迅速变化，而剩余工作岗位的要求也将迅速变化。

sentences.en: Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022.
sentences.cn: 世界经济论坛的研究发现，到 2022 年，各类职业中平均 42% 的"核心技能"将发生变化。

sentences.en: That is a very short timeline.
sentences.cn: 这是非常短的时间。

sentences.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one.
sentences.cn: "谁该为再培训付费"是一个棘手的问题。

sentences.en: For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are.
sentences.cn: 对各公司来说，解雇技能过时的员工、用掌握紧缺技能的人取而代之，这一直是个有吸引力的办法。

words.meaning: n. 诱惑，诱惑人的东西

sentences.en: That does not always happen.
sentences.cn: 当然，这也并非必然。

sentences.en: AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy.
sentences.cn: 美国电话电报公司（AT&T）便常常被奉为（反其道而行之的）完美范例，该公司采用了大规模的技能再培训方案，而非"先裁后聘"的策略。

words.meaning: 作为标杆的典范，黄金标准

sentences.en: Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans.
sentences.cn: 其他包括亚马逊和迪士尼在内的公司也已承诺会制定各自的方案。

words.meaning: v. 承诺，发誓（pledge 的过去分词）

sentences.en: When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle.
sentences.cn: 不过，在更宏观的经济层面看待技能不匹配这一现象时，人们往往将焦点投向政府，希望由其来解决这一问题。

sentences.en: Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
sentences.cn: 当前，加拿大及其他地方所作的努力充其量只能说是迟缓无力的，结果造成了这样一个局面：即便是在高失业率时期和地区，我们也经常听到雇主急缺员工。

words.meaning: adj. 迟缓无力的，慢悠悠的

sentences.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed.
sentences.cn: 由于疫情，失业率的确居高不下。

sentences.en: In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.
sentences.cn: 二月份，加拿大和美国的失业率分别为 3.5% 和 5.5%，处于近二三十年低点，员工短缺问题遍布各地。

sentences.en: As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so.
sentences.cn: 到了五月，两国的失业率飙升至 13.3% 和 13.7%。尽管许多员工短缺问题已不复存在，但并非都是如此。

words.meaning: v. 消失（disappear 的过去分词）

sentences.en: In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
sentences.cn: 举个显而易见的例子，在医疗领域，疫情表明医生、护士以及其他医务人员仍然处于明显短缺状态。

words.meaning: adj. 明显的，显而易见的

sentences.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it.
sentences.cn: 当然，这并不是说我们可以收下一个失业的服务员，不管谁来为此付钱，在几周内把他培训成医生。

sentences.en: But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.
sentences.cn: 但是，即使不能弥合这个缺口，我们或许可以弥合其他缺口，这样做将对相关各方都有利。

sentences.en: That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff.
sentences.cn: 瑞典的情况似乎就是如此：北欧航空公司 90% 的空乘人员被迫休假后，该公司决定启动一项短期再培训方案，重新培训下岗员工来支援医护人员。

words.meaning: v. 使被迫休假，使暂时下岗

sentences.en: The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
sentences.cn: 这是一项集体行动，其他公司以及一所瑞典大学也参与其中。

words.meaning: v. 涉及，使参与（involve 的过去式）

questions.stem: Research by the World Economic Forum suggests ___.
questions.stem_cn: 世界经济论坛的研究表明___。

options.B: an urgent demand for new job skills
options.C: a steady growth of job opportunities

options_cn.B: 对新工作技能的需求迫切

questions.explanation: 定位首段③句：世界经济论坛研究称到 2022 年各职业平均 42% 核心技能将变，末句强调"时间非常短"，即对新技能需求迫切，B 正确（demand for new job skills 同义转述 core skills will change，urgent 对应 a very short timeline）。A 用首段①句 would-be workers 曲解为"全职就业增多"；C 把"所需技能迅速变化"曲解为"就业机会稳步增长"；D"核心技能存在争议"无中生有。

questions.stem: AT&T is cited to show ___.
questions.stem_cn: 文中引用美国电话电报公司是为了说明___。

options.A: an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy
options.B: an immediate need for government support
options.C: the importance of staff appraisal standards

options_cn.C: 工作人员考核标准的重要性

questions.explanation: 第二段②句述多数公司"先裁后聘"惯常做法，③句转折，④句以 AT&T 为例（采取大规模再培训而非先裁后聘），故引用 AT&T 意在说明先裁后聘策略的替代方案，A 正确。B 属政府/宏观层面另一角度；C 由 gold standard 杂糅捏造"考核标准"；D 作者引 AT&T 意在替代常规策略，而非介绍再培训方案特点。

questions.stem: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada ___.
questions.stem_cn: 为解决技能不匹配问题，加拿大所作的努力___。
questions.explanation: 定位第二段末句：加拿大等地努力"充其量迟缓无力"，导致高失业率时期雇主仍急缺员工，即努力仍然不够，D 正确（同义改写 languid at best）。A 由结果臆断"劳动力成本上升"，文中未提；B 把"矛盾局面"偷换为"努力本身自相矛盾"；C 主观臆测"遭强烈反对"，无据。

questions.stem: We can learn from Paragraph 3 that there was ___.
questions.stem_cn: 从第三段我们得知，___是存在的。
questions.explanation: 定位第三段④句：医疗领域医生、护士及其他医务人员仍明显短缺，C 正确（同义改写）。A"调整政策的呼声"文中未提；B 把"用工需求变化"窜改为"雇佣惯例变化"；D 与失业率由低飙高、经济低迷的事实相悖。

questions.stem: Scandinavian Airlines decided to ___.
questions.stem_cn: 北欧航空公司决定___。

options.A: create job vacancies for the unemployed
options.B: prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs
options.C: retrain their cabin staff for better services

options_cn.A: 为失业人员创造空缺职位
options_cn.B: 为其下岗员工从事其他工作提供培训
options_cn.C: 重新培训空乘人员以提升服务
options_cn.D: 为其员工的大学教育提供资金

questions.explanation: 定位末段③句：北欧航空重新培训下岗员工以支援医护人员，B 正确（prepare...for other jobs 对应 reskilled...to support hospital staff）。A 曲解为公司内部造岗；C 扩大培训对象、窜改目的为"提升服务"；D 误读"一所瑞典大学参与"为资助员工上大学。

articles.title: Brexit Ideas of UK Food Self-Sufficiency Are Just Pipe Dreams
articles.topic: 英国靠脱欧实现粮食自给自足只是白日梦：受土地与自然条件所限并不可行
articles.source: 2021 年考研英语（二）Text 2 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.
sentences.cn: 预计到 2050 年，全球人口将多达近 100 亿，预测若要跟上步伐，某些地区的农业产量需接近翻倍，因此，粮食保障问题正越来越多地占据头条新闻。

sentences.en: In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
sentences.cn: 在英国，它最近也成了重大议题，原因相当独特：脱欧。

sentences.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food.
sentences.cn: 脱欧被一些人视为扭转"英国粮食进口"这一新近趋势的契机。

sentences.en: The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s.
sentences.cn: 上世纪 80 年代末，英国生产的粮食占其食用总量的近 3/4，而现在则下滑到了仅 60%。

words.meaning: v. 生产（produce 的第三人称单数）

sentences.en: A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health.
sentences.cn: 这些人的观点为，恢复自给自足将会促进农业发展、加强政治主权，甚至提升国民健康。

sentences.en: Sounds great - but how feasible is this vision?
sentences.cn: 听起来很棒——但这一愿景的可行性如何？

sentences.en: According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production.
sentences.cn: 英国利兹大学关于"英国粮食生产"的报告中指出，英国土地总面积的 85% 与肉类及奶制品的生产相关联。

sentences.en: That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
sentences.cn: 这供应了英国所消费食物的 80%，所以即便让畜牧场覆盖全国，也无法满足我们全部的肉类及奶制品需求。

words.meaning: v. 供应（supply 的第三人称单数）
v. 消费，消耗（consume 的过去分词）

sentences.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave.
sentences.cn: 虽然有许多就这些数据局限性的提醒，但它们所反映的形势仍旧严峻。

words.meaning: n. 提醒，警告（caveat 的复数）
n. 数据，数字（figure 的复数）

sentences.en: To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively - meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
sentences.cn: 英国若想大幅提高自给率，就要急剧减少食用动物性食品，并且或许还需要更集约地从事农业活动——这意味着绿色原野减少、工厂式生产增加。

sentences.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help.
sentences.cn: 但转向以植物为主的饮食也不会有太大意义。

sentences.en: There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis.
sentences.cn: 英国畜牧业占大头是有充分理由的：它的大部分地带都不具备适宜商业化种植的土壤和气候。

sentences.en: Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
sentences.cn: 全国只有 25% 的土地适合作物栽培，而且其中大部分都已经成为耕地了。

sentences.en: Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg - which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes - we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
sentences.cn: 就算我们把所有条件适宜的土地都变成果蔬园地——这会牵扯到取消所有的自然保护区以及让成千上万的人们搬离家园——我们能实现的粮食产量增长也只有 30% 而已。

words.meaning: v. 转变，改变（convert 的过去式）

sentences.en: Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs.
sentences.cn: 如今英国人食用的果蔬中仅有 23% 产自本国，所以，哪怕采用最极端的手段，我们也只能满足鲜果蔬需求的 30%。

words.meaning: adj. 本国产的，本地种植的

sentences.en: That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
sentences.cn: 而在此之后，我们还得再找地方来种植谷物、糖类、籽类、油类等，它们提供了我们当前摄入的大部分卡路里。

questions.stem: Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would ___.
questions.stem_cn: 有些人提出，英国粮食的自给自足将会___。

options.A: be hindered by its population growth
options.C: become a priority of the government
options.D: pose a challenge to its farming industry

questions.explanation: 定位第二段①③句：some 认为恢复自给自足将促进农业、加强政治主权、甚至提升国民健康，B 正确（contribute to well-being 对应 boost the nation's health）。A 用首段全球人口捏造关联；C 曲解"政治主权"为政府优先事项；D 把"促进农业"颠倒为"挑战农业"。

questions.stem: The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK ___.
questions.stem_cn: 利兹大学的报告显示，在英国___。

options.C: most land is used for meat and dairy production
options.D: more green fields will be converted for farming

options_cn.C: 大部分土地被用于肉类和奶制品生产
options_cn.D: 将有更多绿色原野被转为耕作用地

questions.explanation: 定位第三段①句报告内容：英国 85% 土地与肉奶生产相关，即大部分土地用于肉奶生产，C 正确。A、B、D 均出自第四段作者"基于报告的设想"而非报告本身，且 A 属错误推导、B 属曲解。

questions.stem: Crop-growing in the UK is restricted due to ___.
questions.stem_cn: 英国的作物种植因___而受限。
questions.explanation: 定位第五段②句：英国大部分地带不具备适宜商业化种植的土壤和气候，即受自然条件限制，C 正确（natural conditions 概括 the right soil or climate）。A 由"工厂式生产"臆断；B 颠倒因果（畜牧为主是结果非原因）；D 利用 commercial basis 曲解为"商业利益限制种植"。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that British people ___.
questions.stem_cn: 从末段可知，英国人___。

options.A: rely largely on imports for fresh produce
options.B: enjoy a steady rise in fruit consumption
options.C: are seeking effective ways to cut calorie intake
options.D: are trying to grow new varieties of grains

options_cn.A: 主要依靠进口新鲜农产品
options_cn.C: 正寻求有效措施来减少卡路里摄入
options_cn.D: 正试图种植新的谷物类型

questions.explanation: 定位末段①句：仅 23% 果蔬产自本国，可合理推算其余大部分依赖进口，A 正确。B 误解 23%/30% 两个数据含义；C、D 把②句假设性情形（另找地方种谷物）曲解为英国人的现实行动。

questions.stem: The author's attitude to food self-sufficiency in the UK is ___.
questions.stem_cn: 作者对英国粮食自给自足的态度是___。
questions.explanation: 全文脉络为层层让步否定（第二段末设问质疑、第三/五段极端假设仍不可行、第六段雪上加霜），作者对英国粮食自给自足持怀疑（doubtful）态度，B 正确。A、D 混淆他人观点与作者观点；C 误读让步表达为容忍，作者实为以极端假设强调不可行。

articles.title: Big Tech's 'Buy and Kill' Tactics Come Under Scrutiny
articles.topic: 大型科技公司的"买了即杀"策略受审查：恶意收购扼杀潜在竞争对手
articles.source: 2021 年考研英语（二）Text 3 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.
sentences.cn: 2015 年，微软收购任务管理应用 Wunderlist 和移动日历 Sunrise 时，挑选的是当时在硅谷名声大噪的两家新科技公司。

words.meaning: n. 新来者，新手（newcomer 的复数）

sentences.en: Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for "productivity" software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
sentences.cn: 微软自创的 Office 在"生产效率"软件市场独占鳌头，而这两家初创企业则代表了智能手机领域全新科技的一股新潮。

words.meaning: v. 占支配地位（dominate 的第三人称单数）
n. 初创企业（start-up 的复数）

sentences.en: Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.
sentences.cn: 然而，这两款应用后来都被下架了，微软表示已将其最佳性能融入到了自身产品中。

words.meaning: v. 取消，报废（scrap 的过去分词）
n. 特色，特点（feature 的复数）

sentences.en: Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many "acqui-hires" that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
sentences.cn: 两款应用的工程师团队留了下来，使之成为大型科技公司为弥补科技人才紧缺而进行的众多"人才并购"的两例。

sentences.en: To Microsoft's critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
sentences.cn: 在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist 和 Sunrise 的命运表明：科技巨头会无情地蚕食一切阻碍其发展的创新公司。

words.meaning: n. 批评者（critic 的复数）

sentences.en: "They bought the seedlings and closed them down," complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.
sentences.cn: 总部位于旧金山的 Switch 风险投资公司合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨道，"他们买下这些初创企业然后将其关闭"，将那些有朝一日可能会成长为竞争对手的企业扼杀于摇篮。

words.meaning: v. 抱怨，埋怨（complain 的过去式）

sentences.en: Microsoft declined to comment.
sentences.cn: 微软拒绝对此置评。

words.meaning: v. 谢绝，婉言拒绝（decline 的过去式）

sentences.en: Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: "I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.
sentences.cn: 和其他初创企业投资者一样，阿诺德的公司也常常依赖于将初创企业出售给大型科技公司，不过对于收购结局他内心五味杂陈："自私一点说，我认为这些收购对我有利。

sentences.en: But are they good for the American economy?
sentences.cn: 但它们对美国经济有利吗？

sentences.en: I don't know."
sentences.cn: 我不知道。"

sentences.en: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.
sentences.cn: 美国联邦贸易委员会表示希望找到这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
sentences.cn: 本周，委员会要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年内进行的诸多小型收购的相关信息。

words.meaning: 市值最高的，最有价值的

sentences.en: Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
sentences.cn: 尽管在现阶段这项要求只是一个研究项目，却让人们燃起了希望：监管机构开始介入此前不曾涉足的早期科技市场。

sentences.en: Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals - many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise - might seem beside the point.
sentences.cn: 鉴于这五家科技公司的总市值超过 5.5 万亿美元，匆忙审查这些小额收购（其中许多远没有 Wunderlist、Sunrise 收购案引人注目）似乎有些避重就轻的味道。

sentences.en: Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years - a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
sentences.cn: 过去的五年中，这五大科技公司加起来平均每年只花 34 亿美元用于 10 亿美元以下的收购。这个数额同他们庞大的资金储备以及去年在美国完成的 1300 多亿美元的风险投资相比，无异于沧海一粟。

sentences.en: However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a "buy and kill" tactic to simply close them down.
sentences.cn: 但批评人士认为，这些大公司利用这样的交易，在最具危险性的潜在竞争对手有机会形成势头之前将他们买下，有些时候就是"买了即杀"策略中的一步，就是要让他们关门。

questions.stem: What is true about Wunderlist and Sunrise after their acquisitions?
questions.stem_cn: Wunderlist 和 Sunrise 被收购后的真实情况如何？

options_cn.C: 他们的科技性能得到提升。
options_cn.D: 他们的产品被重新定价。

questions.explanation: 定位第二段②句：软件被下架，但工程师团队留了下来（stayed on），即工程师被留用，A 正确。B 张冠李戴（市值巨大说的是五巨头）；C 性能提升的是微软自家产品；D"重新定价"与"已下架"矛盾。

questions.stem: Microsoft's critics believe that the big tech companies tend to ___.
questions.stem_cn: 微软的批评者认为，大型科技公司往往会___。

options_cn.B: 消灭他们的潜在竞争对手
options_cn.C: 不公正地对待新技术人才

questions.explanation: 定位第三段①②句：批评者称科技巨头无情蚕食挡道的创新公司、抢在其成长为竞争对手前将其扼杀，即消灭潜在竞争对手，B 正确。A、C、D 或断章取义或反向窜改，且均非"批评者观点"。

questions.stem: Paul Arnold is concerned that small acquisitions might ___.
questions.stem_cn: 保罗·阿诺德担忧，小额收购可能会___。

options_cn.D: 挫伤初创企业投资者的信心

questions.explanation: 定位第四段③④句：阿诺德坦言收购对自己有利，但反问"它们对美国经济有利吗？我不知道"，透露对国家经济受损的担忧，C 正确。A、B 与其"巩固垄断、阻碍新竞争"的判断相悖；D 与"对投资者有利"相悖。

questions.stem: The US Federal Trade Commission intends to ___.
questions.stem_cn: 美国联邦贸易委员会想要___。
questions.explanation: 定位第五段①②句：FTC 为寻找"是否有害经济"的答案，要求五大科技公司提供过去十年小额收购的信息，即审查小额收购，C 正确。A 属过度推导；B 对 research project 断章取义；D 监管对象搞错（是收购行为而非初创企业运营）。

questions.stem: For the five biggest tech companies, their small acquisitions have ___.
questions.stem_cn: 对五家最大的科技公司而言，他们的小额收购___。

options.C: set an example for future deals

options_cn.A: 没有带来多少财务压力
options_cn.B: 没有带来多少管理问题
options_cn.C: 为后来的交易树立了榜样

questions.explanation: 定位第六段②句：五巨头每年合计仅约 34 亿美元用于 10 亿美元以下收购，与庞大资金储备和逾 1300 亿美元风投相比是"沧海一粟"，即几乎未带来财务压力，A 正确。B 管理问题文中未提；C 由 examples 望文生义；D 利润与小额收购的因果系捏造。

articles.title: Sometimes the Heart Is Smarter Than the Head
articles.topic: 直觉有时比深思更准确：在处理社会信息等特定情境下深思反而干扰判断
articles.source: 2021 年考研英语（二）Text 4 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.
sentences.cn: 我们很擅长运用第一印象——"经验薄片"来评判他人（从对照片的一瞥，到长达五分钟的互动都可称为"经验薄片"），此时深思不仅没有必要，而且会造成干扰。

sentences.en: In one study of the ability she called "thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness.
sentences.cn: 在纳里尼·安巴迪称为"行为薄片撷取"能力的一项研究中，这位已故的心理学家要求参与者观看教授们（授课）的 10 秒无声视频片段，并对教师的整体效果进行评分。

words.meaning: 行为薄片撷取（基于极少信息迅速判断）

sentences.en: Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings.
sentences.cn: 他们的评分与学生在学期末（对教师）的评分高度相关。

sentences.en: Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.
sentences.cn: 另一组参与者在观看视频片段时需要从 1000 开始以 9 为单位倒数，这占用了他们的意识工作记忆。

words.meaning: v. 占用（occupy 的现在分词）

sentences.en: Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
sentences.cn: 这组人的评分也同样准确，这显示出"社会信息处理"的直觉性。

sentences.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.
sentences.cn: 极为关键的是，另一组参与者被要求在评分之前花一分钟写下他们做出判断的原因。

words.meaning: ad. 极为关键地，很大程度上

sentences.en: Accuracy dropped dramatically.
sentences.cn: 此时，评分的准确性大幅下降。

sentences.en: Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
sentences.cn: 安巴迪推测，深思使参与者将精力集中于那些生动但具有误导性的信号（比如特定的手势或说话方式），而未能让微妙信号间的复杂关系形成整体印象。

words.meaning: v. 推测，怀疑（suspect 的过去式）
生动但有误导性的信号
n. 相互影响，相互作用

sentences.en: She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
sentences.cn: 她发现，参与者在观看 15 秒的双人视频片段，然后判断两者是陌生人、朋友还是约会对象时，也会受到类似的干扰。

sentences.en: Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection.
sentences.cn: 其他研究表明，我们在依靠直觉而非深思时，更能从"行为薄片"中察觉出欺骗。

sentences.en: "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing.
sentences.cn: "这就像你在开手动挡汽车，"东北大学心理学家朱迪斯·霍尔说，"如果你开始反复思考如何挂挡，你就会忘记自己本来是要做什么。

sentences.en: But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine.
sentences.cn: 但如果你不假思索地按照习惯操作，就不会遇到什么问题。

sentences.en: Much of our social life is like that."
sentences.cn: 我们的社交生活也多半如此。"

sentences.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.
sentences.cn: 考虑得过多也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。

sentences.en: College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale.
sentences.cn: 在不要求大学生细察其依据的情况下，他们对草莓果酱和大学课程的评估与专家的意见更一致。

words.meaning: 分析其（评判的）理由依据

sentences.en: And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex - when they had a lot of information to process.
sentences.cn: 而在人们被要求关注感受而非细节时，做出的购车决定会在客观上更合适，而且更令自己满意，但也只有在这一决定很复杂的情况下方才如此——（因为）此时人们有很多信息需要处理。

sentences.en: Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.
sentences.cn: 直觉的特殊能力只有在特定的情境下才会发挥出来。

words.meaning: v. 突然释放，使爆发（unleash 的过去分词）

sentences.en: In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).
sentences.cn: 在一项研究中，参与者完成了一组八项任务，其中四项运用了深度思索能力（辨识规则、理解词汇），另外四项运用了直觉与创造力（创造新产品或修辞格）。

words.meaning: v. 利用（已有的资源、能力等）（tap 的过去式）
深度思索能力，反思性思维

sentences.en: Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," "hunches," "my heart").
sentences.cn: 而后，他们对自己使用直觉（"本能""预感""内心"）的程度给出了评分。

words.meaning: n. 预感，直觉（hunch 的复数）

sentences.en: Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
sentences.cn: 不出所料，使用直觉损害了他们在前四项任务中的表现，而对其余的任务则有所帮助。

sentences.en: Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
sentences.cn: 有时候，心比脑更聪明。

words.meaning: 头脑（此处代指思维能力）

questions.stem: Nalini Ambady's study deals with ___.
questions.stem_cn: 纳里尼·安巴迪的研究涉及___。
questions.explanation: 定位第一、二段：安巴迪"行为薄片撷取"研究让参与者凭 10 秒无声视频（第一印象）为教师评分并与学生期末评分对比，考察的是第一印象的可靠性，B 正确。A 由"工作记忆"断章取义；C 对师生互动强加关联；D 误读实验干扰设置。

questions.stem: In Ambady's study, rating accuracy dropped when participants ___.
questions.stem_cn: 在安巴迪的研究中，当参与者___时，评分的准确率下降。

options.B: gave the rating in limited time

options_cn.B: 在限定时间内进行评分

questions.explanation: 定位第二段①③句：被要求写下评分理由（先深思）的一组准确性大幅下降；安巴迪推测深思使人聚焦生动但有误导性的细节信号（手势、说话方式），A 正确（focused on specific details 对应 focused them on vivid but misleading cues）。B 误把"花一分钟写理由"当作限时评分；C 视频时长非变量重点；D"相互讨论"原文无据。

questions.stem: Judith Hall mentions driving to show that ___.
questions.stem_cn: 朱迪斯·霍尔提及驾驶是为了表明___。

options_cn.A: 深思熟虑有时反会让人分心
options_cn.C: 社交技能须经培养才能获得

questions.explanation: 定位第三段②③句：霍尔以开手动挡汽车作类比——反复琢磨挂挡就会忘记本来要做什么，凭习惯操作反而顺利，说明深思会分散注意力、干扰判断，A 正确。B 对"忘记在做什么"断章取义；C 未论及社交技能培养；D 与首句"直觉更能察觉欺骗"方向相反。

questions.stem: When you are making complex decisions, it is advisable to ___.
questions.stem_cn: 当你在做复杂的决定时，明智的做法是___。
questions.explanation: 定位第四段末句：当决定复杂（信息量大）时，关注感受而非细节做出的购车决定客观上更好、主观上更满意，故应遵从感觉，D 正确（follow your feelings 对应 focus on their feelings）。A 与原意恰相反；B 误解首句语义重心；C 由"专家意见"碎片信息捏造。

questions.stem: What can we learn from the last paragraph?
questions.stem_cn: 从最后一段我们可以得知什么？

options_cn.B: 直觉可能会影响思考性工作。
options_cn.D: 客观思维可提升直觉力。

questions.explanation: 定位末段④句：使用直觉损害了参与者在四项深思型任务（辨识规则、理解词汇）中的表现，即直觉可能影响思考性工作，B 正确。A 创造新产品的耗时未提；C 张冠李戴（理解词汇属深思任务而非创造力任务）；D 提升直觉力的方法文中未论及。
